column1: # TITLE: Expression data comparing azacitidine and decitabine in non-small cell lung cancer lines

# SUMMARY: Azacitidine (AZA) and decitabine (DAC) are cytidine azanucleoside analogs with clinical activity in myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) and potential activity in solid tumors. To better understand the mechanism of action of these drugs
column2: we examined the effects of AZA and DAC in a panel of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cell lines. Of 5 NSCLC lines tested in a cell viability assay
column3: all were sensitive to AZA (EC50 of 1.8–10.5 µM)
column4: while only H1299 cells were equally sensitive to DAC (EC50 of 5.1 µM). In the relatively DAC-insensitive cell line A549
column5: both AZA and DAC caused DNA methyltransferase I depletion and DNA hypomethylation; however
column6: only AZA significantly induced markers of DNA damage and apoptosis
column7: suggesting that mechanisms in addition to
column9: DNA hypomethylation are important for AZA-induced cell death. Cell cycle analysis indicated that AZA induced an accumulation of cells in sub-G1 phase
column10: whereas DAC mainly caused an increase of cells in G2/M. Gene expression analysis of AZA- and DAC-treated cells revealed strikingly different profiles
column11: with many genes distinctly regulated by each drug. In summary
column12: while both AZA and DAC caused DNA hypomethylation
column13: distinct effects were demonstrated on regulation of gene expression
